name: Kestrel Electrical
short: An electrician's page built as a fuse board — every job is a breaker.
long: Three lines say what they do, where they go and when they answer; under them sit three fields and the phone number at poster size. The services are a row of breakers on a board — flip one and it turns on to show what's included, what it costs and a button to ring about it. The only thing that moves on the page is a switch.
proves: Someone standing in a dark kitchen can ring the right number in one tap, at any hour, without reading a word of marketing.
features: Seven breakers on a consumer unit — fault finding, fuse board, EV charger, rewire, EICR, sockets, emergency — each flipping on to its own panel
The main switch is the phone number, and it swaps between the office line and the emergency mobile from the real clock
Callback form that validates and confirms by name, number and the hour the office will ring
Postcode outward-code check across NG1–NG17, and a sticky CALL / BOOK bar on phones
story: Most trade sites bury the number under a hero image and a form nobody fills in. Borrowing the layout of the thing an electrician opens every day made the page label itself: everything is a switch, and the biggest one rings the phone.
